subject: Archaeology
subcategory: Lost Cities of the Ancient World
title: Heracleion: Egypt's Sunken Port
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Heracleion: Egypt's Sunken Port.

hook.text: An entire Egyptian port city lay hidden under the Mediterranean Sea for 1,200 years before divers found it.

buildup.text: Heracleion was Egypt's main trading port before Alexandria was built. Greek historians described it as magnificent.

discovery.text: In 2000, Franck Goddio found temples, giant statues, and 64 ships lying on the seabed in Abu Qir Bay.

twist.text: The city sank because it was built on unstable clay. Earthquakes and rising seas did the rest over centuries.

climax.text: Divers pulled up a five-meter granite statue of a pharaoh from the mud — perfectly preserved by the cold dark water.

punchline.text: The sea swallowed a city whole and kept it in near-perfect condition.

quiz.question: Why did the ancient city of Heracleion sink?
options: A massive tsunami overwhelmed the city in a single event
It was built on unstable clay that gave way during earthquakes
Rising sea levels from melting glaciers flooded the coastline
